description: Ralph Loop Phase 1 context-load sequence worked without a SKILL.md file. README.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, CONTROL_LAYER.md, DEPLOYMENT.md, and all SQL files provided sufficient context to complete the session without data loss.
context: SKILL.md was listed in the Ralph Loop prompt as a required context item but does not exist in this repository.
lesson: The Ralph Loop context checklist includes SKILL.md as item 1, but the remaining 5 items (architecture docs + SQL files) are sufficient for a quality-hardening pass. A missing SKILL.md is a gap but not a blocker.
recommendation: Create a SKILL.md at the repository root that summarises the Ralph Loop methodology, the 10 failure patterns, the 5-view architecture, and the memory system structure. This will make future sessions self-contained.

description: CP-5 (ISNUMERIC ban) grep produced false positives — all hits were in comment/changelog lines referencing the fix. A secondary check using node (parse non-comment lines only) confirmed zero active ISNUMERIC() calls.
context: Standard grep -r 'ISNUMERIC' reported matches in changelog lines like '-- replaced ISNUMERIC with TRY_CAST'. Initial result was FAIL; detailed analysis showed PASS.
lesson: The CP-5 validation script in the Ralph Loop prompt uses a plain grep that cannot distinguish comments from code. Always perform a secondary check that filters comment lines when running the ISNUMERIC ban check.
recommendation: Update the validate-sql.sh script to use a line-level comment filter: strip everything after '--' before testing for ISNUMERIC. Or use a pattern like grep -v '^[[:space:]]*--' to exclude pure-comment lines.

description: Config CTE pattern using scalar subqueries (SELECT value FROM Config) works cleanly in SQL Server views for all use cases: WHERE clauses, CASE expressions, DATEADD arguments, and scalar arithmetic.
context: sql/03_etb_wfq_pipe.sql and pipeline-views/03_etb_wfq_pipe.sql use the same pattern. Validated that CROSS JOIN Config in the FROM clause allows Config columns to be referenced directly in all contexts without correlated subquery overhead.
lesson: For views with a CROSS JOIN Config, use direct column reference (e.g. Config.Lot_Age_Limit_Days). For views without CROSS JOIN Config (where Config is only referenced in scalar subqueries), use (SELECT value FROM Config) syntax. Both patterns are correct; choose based on whether Config columns appear in GROUP BY scope.
recommendation: When the Config CTE is referenced in GROUP BY or SELECT list expressions alongside aggregate functions, prefer CROSS JOIN Config and direct column reference to avoid the overhead of repeated correlated scalar subqueries.

description: The sql/ and pipeline-views/ directories contain near-duplicate files. sql/ is the production deployment target; pipeline-views/ is the hardened reference. They have diverged in quality — pipeline-views/ is ahead on Config CTEs and documentation. Future sessions should synchronise both directories in the same pass to prevent re-accumulating the gap.
context: sql/03_etb_wfq_pipe.sql lacked Config CTE while pipeline-views/03_etb_wfq_pipe.sql had it. The same divergence exists for Views 1, 2, 4, 5 between the two directories.
lesson: Treating sql/ and pipeline-views/ as separate maintenance targets creates audit confusion. One of the two should be the canonical source and the other should be generated or explicitly tagged as legacy.
recommendation: Designate pipeline-views/ as the canonical source. On the next pass, overwrite sql/01 through sql/05 from pipeline-views/ after verifying no sql/-specific overrides exist. Add a README note explaining the directory relationship.

description: Ralph Loop 4-phase execution with 14 checkpoints completed cleanly in a single session. Phases 1 and 2 produced a clear, auditable change set. Phase 3 PR was created with a full checklist template. Phase 4 memory logging provides traceability for future agents.
context: First full Ralph Loop session executed in this repository. Total files modified: 5 SQL files + 1 SCOPE.md created + 1 decisions/ directory created with 2 JSONL log files.
lesson: The Ralph Loop methodology is well-suited to quality-hardening passes where changes are additive (Config CTEs, documentation) and carry no business logic risk. The 14-checkpoint verification gate provides high confidence without a live database connection.
recommendation: Schedule a second Ralph Loop pass to: (1) synchronise sql/01-05 from pipeline-views/, (2) add Config CTE to sql/02_etb_wc_inv_unified.sql if it lacks one, (3) create SKILL.md at repo root.
